course_references.use: Simple random sampling without replacement, selection mechanism, sample size and sampling variability.
P-value meaning, alpha decision, failure to reject and permutation comparisons.
Chi-square independence, Welch and paired t tests, assumptions and practical significance.
A p-value alone does not prove causality. Randomly sampling hosts is not randomly assigning a treatment.

design.reason: 10,000 hosts give several thousand observations per recorded class while using under 5% of the eligible host frame. This provides a manageable common sample for all questions. The size was fixed before comparing p-values; it is a teaching sensitivity analysis, not a formal power calculation or an optimal size prescribed by the slides.
design.selection: pandas sample(n=10000, replace=False, random_state=42), applied once to the existing one-URL-per-consistent-host frame. Every host has inclusion probability 10000/N. Selection does not balance classes or depend on feature values or p-values.
design.scope: The population frame is the 220,023 eligible exact hosts in this benchmark. It is not all websites on the internet. The original frame covers every eligible host, with one randomly selected URL per host; it is not a random subset of those hosts.
design.limitations: The sample is nested in the reference frame, so agreement is a sensitivity check, not independent replication. Sampling cannot repair source collection bias, campaign dependence or multiple exploratory testing. Reference p-values are retained as the original superpopulation-model calculations; finite benchmark population differences can instead be described directly. Conventional tests are repeated without a finite-population correction to preserve the original methods; the sample fraction is below 5%.
design.pairing: Q12 uses only phishing hosts within the common sample and keeps the two scores paired. Q15 keeps both rule outcomes per selected host. Q11 fixes the original ten TLD groups plus Other. Q13–Q14 keep their original 3,000-host reference and repeat the same 1,999-shuffle tests using the class counts observed in the shared 10,000-host sample.
design.p_values: Scientific-notation tail probabilities are numerical approximations. Underflowed t/chi-square tails are computed on a scaled log scale, preserving the same statistic and distribution. Permutation p-values remain (extreme + 1)/2000, with minimum 0.0005; this resolution is not improved by scientific notation.
